skill.name: dependency-management-deps-audit
skill.description: Analyze project dependencies for vulnerabilities, license obligations, outdated packages, supply chain risk, and prioritized remediation steps.
skill.summary: Guides dependency security, license, and upgrade audits for software projects.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and filesystem detections are false positives from Markdown or JavaScript template syntax. Confirmed issues are low-risk outbound registry lookups and a medium-risk automated remediation example that can modify dependency files; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Automated remediation can run forceful dependency updates.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npm audit fix --force or similar commands, and prefer dry-run output before changes.

remediation.issue: Dependency scans contact third-party registries and analysis services.
remediation.suggestion: Document each external service and ask before sending private package names, versions, or component coordinates.

remediation.issue: Shell examples mix analysis, changes, testing, and rollback in one flow.
remediation.suggestion: Separate report generation from remediation steps, and recommend a dedicated branch with reviewed diffs for dependency changes.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 468 is a JavaScript template literal inside a Markdown code example for a Bundlephobia URL. It is not Ruby backtick execution or shell command execution.
Line 491 formats a JavaScript string for bundle size display inside documentation. It does not execute a shell command.
Line 496 logs an error message with a JavaScript template literal. There is no shell invocation or command substitution.
Line 748 uses a JavaScript template literal to create a GitHub issue title. The code calls a documented GitHub API helper and does not execute a shell command.
The command substitution reads a numeric field from a local npm-audit.json file in a GitHub Actions example. It has no user-controlled shell construction or injection path in the shown context.
The command substitution only interpolates a jq result into a CI error message from a local audit file. This is a fixed diagnostic command, not arbitrary command execution.
This starts a Bash remediation example that later runs package-manager and git commands. The usage is legitimate, but agent-guided shell execution can modify project dependencies and lockfiles.
The fetch call contacts Bundlephobia for dependency size analysis. This is expected behavior, but it sends package names and versions to a third-party service.
Line 562 lists common package names including axios for typosquatting checks. It does not import or invoke an HTTP client library.
The Python example posts package metadata to the npm advisory API. This is a legitimate vulnerability lookup but still performs outbound network communication.
The URL points to the npm security advisory endpoint used for vulnerability checks. It is a legitimate service, but private package data could be disclosed if used without consent.
The PyPI API URL is used for dependency metadata checks. It is a normal registry endpoint, but use can reveal queried package names.
The RubyGems API URL is used for package metadata lookup. It is legitimate, but it is still outbound communication to a third-party registry.
The Sonatype OSS Index URL is a known component vulnerability reporting service. The risk is low but real because component coordinates may be sent externally.
The hardcoded npm advisory API endpoint is actively used by the requests.post call. This is expected vulnerability scanning behavior with a low data-disclosure risk.
The Bundlephobia URL is used to query package size data. It is legitimate but can expose dependency names and versions to a third-party service.
Line 234 is a Python for loop over vulnerability objects. The word pattern does not create hard links or perform filesystem operations.
Line 669 is a Markdown checklist item saying all tests pass. It has no network scanning, host discovery, or reconnaissance behavior.
Line 35 uses Markdown inline code to reference a resource file path. It does not execute Ruby, shell, or any command.
Line 44 uses Markdown inline code for a documentation path. It is a resource reference, not command execution.

content.value_statement: Dependency issues can expose products to vulnerabilities, license conflicts, and supply chain risk. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through audits, upgrade planning, and remediation reports.
actual_capabilities: Guides inventory of direct and transitive dependencies from common manifest files.
Explains vulnerability checks for npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven, and related registries.
Helps prioritize fixes by severity, exposure, exploit availability, and package usage.
Supports license compliance review with risk categories and remediation notes.
Provides templates for upgrade plans, pull requests, CI audits, and dependency reports.
Highlights supply chain risks such as typosquatting, maintainer changes, and suspicious package metadata.
limitations: It depends on available manifests, lockfiles, and scanner output from the target project.
It does not replace official legal review for license obligations.
Network-based checks may expose package names and versions to registry services.
Automated upgrade commands can break builds and should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Security Review
use_cases.description: Audit dependencies before a production release and produce a prioritized remediation list.

use_cases.title: Plan Dependency Upgrades
use_cases.description: Compare current package versions with safer targets and identify compatibility risks.

use_cases.title: Review License Exposure
use_cases.description: Classify dependency licenses and flag packages that may need legal or policy review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Dependency Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple project review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project for vulnerable, outdated, and risky dependencies. Summarize the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: License Compliance Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Check dependency licenses against team policy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the dependency licenses in this repository. Flag restrictive or unknown licenses and suggest next steps for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritized Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn scanner output into an action plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dependency scan results to create a remediation plan. Include severity, exploitability, upgrade target, test impact, and owner notes.

prompt_templates.title: CI Dependency Monitoring Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe CI workflow for dependency vulnerability monitoring. Include approval points, private package handling, failure rules, and report outputs.

output_examples.input: A repository has package manifests, lockfiles, and npm audit output.
output: The report lists critical and high vulnerabilities first.
Each item includes affected package, current version, fixed version, exposure, and recommended owner.
The plan separates safe patch updates from breaking major upgrades.

output_examples.input: A team asks whether dependency licenses meet policy.
output: The result groups licenses into approved, review needed, and blocked categories.
Packages with unknown licenses are flagged for source review.
The report notes where legal review is required.

output_examples.input: A project needs continuous dependency monitoring.
output: The guidance defines scheduled scans, pull request checks, and alert thresholds.
It recommends human approval before running commands that change dependency files.
It includes a concise remediation workflow for critical findings.

best_practices: Run scans from a clean branch and review every dependency file change.
Confirm scanner findings against official advisories before reporting risk.
Ask before sending private package data to external registry or analysis services.
anti_patterns: Running forceful package updates without reading the proposed dependency changes.
Treating all vulnerability scanner output as exploitable without project context.
Publishing private dependency names or vulnerability details in public channels.

faq.question: Does this skill run scanners by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent through scanner workflows and report creation using the tools available in the workspace.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover?
faq.answer: The playbook includes npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven, Go modules, and common lockfile workflows.

faq.question: Can it fix vulnerabilities automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest remediation steps, but dependency changes should be reviewed before commands are run.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but users should approve any network checks that send package names or versions outside the organization.

faq.question: Does it handle license compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps classify licenses and identify packages that need policy or legal review.

faq.question: Can it replace a security team review?
faq.answer: No. It prepares evidence and remediation plans, but final risk acceptance should stay with the responsible team.
